library(NicheMapR)
library(ecmwfr)
library(mcera5)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(tidync)
library(microclima)
library(keyring)
library(ncdf4)

# get ERA5 data with package mcera5 (just do once for region and time of interest)

# assign your credentials (register here: https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/user/register)

cds_api_key <- "xxxxxxxx"

xmx <- 115
ymn <- 38
ymx <-42

# temporal extent

# filename and location for downloaded .nc files

op <- "/Users/jiangzhongwen/Desktop"

# build a request (covering multiple years)
req <- build_era5_request(xmin = xmn, xmax = xmx,

str(req)

dstart <- "10/07/2020"

messages.subject: Re: Error in microclima:microclimaforNMR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rachel,

It works on my system for that site. You might have an out-of-date version. Can you try again after reinstalling microclima (and perhaps NicheMapR too)? Use

devtools::install_github('ilyamaclean/microclima')
devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR')

Note that once you have it working, you'll see another problem in that the model will crash part way through. This is because of the snow calculations, and you're predicting to quite a snowy region - sudden melting can make things hard for the integrator to solve the soil temperature calculations and you need to make the error tolerance of the integrator - input ERR - greater than the default value of 1.5. I found a value of 2.5 does the trick. So you'd do:

micro <- micro_ncep(loc = longlatex, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, ERR = 2.5)

Note if you use do this:

micro <- micro_ncep(loc = longlatex, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, ERR = 2.5, save = 1)

then it will save the dowloaded NCEP and DEM data locally and then you can run it again for the same time and place but with different parameters without having to wait for it to download by doing this:

micro <- micro_ncep(loc = longlatex, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, ERR = 2.5, save = 2)

All the best,
Mike

> Hi Rachel,
>
> It works on my system for that site. You might have an out-of-date version. Can you try again after reinstalling microclima (and perhaps NicheMapR too)? Use
>
> devtools::install_github('ilyamaclean/microclima')
> devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR')
>
> Note that once you have it working, you'll see another problem in that the model will crash part way through. This is because of the snow calculations, and you're predicting to quite a snowy region - sudden melting can make things hard for the integrator to solve the soil temperature calculations and you need to make the error tolerance of the integrator - input ERR - greater than the default value of 1.5. I found a value of 2.5 does the trick. So you'd do:
>
> micro <- micro_ncep(loc = longlatex, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, ERR = 2.5)
>
> Note if you use do this:
>
> micro <- micro_ncep(loc = longlatex, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, ERR = 2.5, save = 1)
>
> then it will save the dowloaded NCEP and DEM data locally and then you can run it again for the same time and place but with different parameters without having to wait for it to download by doing this:
>
> micro <- micro_ncep(loc = longlatex, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, ERR = 2.5, save = 2)
>
> All the best,
> Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hey Mike,

I’ve been banging my head against the wall on this for a few
weeks now, figured I’d finally ask for your advice!

I’m trying to take DEB parameters estimated from Jorn Bruggeman’s
Debber tool (https://deb.bolding-bruggeman.com/) and apply them in NicheMapR to create plausible models for a group
of given species that don’t have parameters in the AddMyPet database. I’ve
written R code that randomly pulls from the distribution of possible values that
Debber calculates for each species (so for a given species, I randomly pull a single value for the Arrhenius
temperature from a normal distribution between the lower 2.5% and upper 97.5%, same for the log normal distribution for energy
conductance, etc) and runs these parameters through the ectotherm model, then
repeats with a different set of randomly drawn parameters from the
distributions for these variables.

Since these are randomly drawn parameters from these distributions, I would expect to see some results where the model doesn't work. However, I’m pretty much exclusively
seeing absolutely bonkers results, such as an animal burrowing underground and
refusing to come out/starving to death even if burrow = 0 and maxdepth = 1 (and with rock bottom CT_mins, T_RB_min, T_B_min, and T_F_min), starting
at stage 0 (egg) even if explicitly told to start at stage 3 (mature), and
things like that. I’m positive this is a garbage in, garbage out problem, but
for the life of me I can’t figure out what the garbage is. I’ve compared the
values that come out of the random draws for species that are in the AddMyPet database
to the exact values in AddMyPet and they seem approximate to each other.

Have you seen anything like this before/is my basic premise
of using Debber in this way wrong? (I can send you my code but I figured I’d
ask the broader question first in case you had experienced this issue before)

Fingers crossed!

Adam
